claim: Early static ML forecasters were far below the human crowd (65% vs 92% accuracy; calibration error 40% vs 8%).
agent_test: Not needed; historical.

claim: In 2023-24, base GPT-4-class models scored about 0.20-0.21 Brier on crowd-platform questions, barely better than the 0.25 coin-flip, and worse than the human crowd (0.149).
agent_test: Run our agent bare (no scaffold) on a held-out resolved question set; compare to crowd.
audit_note: Minor: Schoenegger and Park GPT-4 0.20 is on only 23 questions and not significantly different from 0.25 (p=0.23); crowd benchmarks differ (0.149 Halawi, 0.07 Schoenegger).

claim: Retrieval plus a fine-tuned reasoner plus ensembling moved a system to 0.179 vs crowd 0.149 (Halawi). Removing both fine-tuning and retrieval returns it to baseline (0.206 vs 0.208).
agent_test: Ablate retrieval and sample-ensemble in our scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: LLM systems beat the crowd only in narrow conditions (crowd uncertain 0.3-0.7). With early retrieval and 5+ articles added, the edge nearly disappears (.240 vs .247); the crowd wins when highly certain.
agent_test: Stratify our results by crowd-uncertainty bin; report per bin.

claim: An LLM crowd (12 models) matched a human crowd of 925 on 31 questions (0.20 vs 0.19, equivalence at d=0.5 bound), with a strong yes-bias (mean 57 percent forecast, only 14 of 31 resolved yes).
agent_test: Sample N diverse runs and take the median; check yes-bias on our agent.

claim: Showing an LLM the human median improves its Brier by 17-28 percent, but a plain average of machine and human median beats the LLM's own update.
agent_test: Test anchoring on an external prior then averaging vs letting the agent update.

claim: ForecastBench (2025): superforecasters 0.096, public 0.121, best LLM 0.122 on a 200-question subset; best LLM without the crowd forecast 0.136; p<0.001 vs supers. Re-verified from the PDF by the cross-checker.
agent_test: Reference numbers only.

claim: Giving the LLM the crowd forecast on market questions is a large part of its edge (0.136 to 0.122); recent news did not help in the original paper.
agent_test: Run with and without a market-price prior and with and without news at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The original linear projection put LLM-superforecaster parity near Arena 1406 (CI 1346-1633) or 6.5e26 FLOP (CI 1e26-9e28); R2 0.47 and 0.41, so the projection is loose.
agent_test: Not a test; weak evidence.
audit_note: Compute CI 9.69e25-8.65e28 is rounded to 1e26-9e28 in the claim; the Lu 2025 source only gives a different projection, so the numbers rest on Karger alone.

claim: Gap to superforecasters grows when combination questions are included (0.054 for GPT-4o, twice the GPT-4 to GPT-4o step); human combo scores assume independence.
agent_test: Add conjunction and consistency checks to our agent's evaluation.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Gap depends on category and horizon: Claude 3.5 Sonnet beat supers on Economics & Business, 30-day and 90-day; lost at 7-day (0.093 vs 0.076).
agent_test: Report per horizon; avoid pooled-only claims.

claim: Agentic search ensembles reached or passed the 2024 superforecaster median on ForecastBench subsets (AIA 0.1076 vs 0.1110; market subset 0.0753 vs 0.0740) but lose to the market on liquid markets (0.1258 vs 0.1106).
agent_test: Replicate agentic search + multi-run mean + Platt scaling at equal tokens.

claim: Agentic search beats non-agentic search, and any search beats none (0.1230 to 0.1140); Platt scaling of the ensemble mean improves Brier (0.1119 to 0.1076 fitted in-distribution; 0.1125 to 0.1104 when fitted on another question set). Murphy (2026) finds Platt gains of +0.72 to +1.48 Brier Index but no statistically resolved gain for one backbone.
agent_test: Add a post-hoc extremising/Platt step to our agent and measure.

claim: Combining LLM with market price beats either alone (0.103 vs 0.116 no-news LLM; 0.075 best configuration).
agent_test: Compare agent alone, price alone, average.

claim: Outcome-reward RL on forecasts (ReMax, GRPO variants) reached 0.190 Brier and better ECE than o1 (0.202), but did not beat the market; plain GRPO collapsed to overconfidence.
agent_test: Not testable without training; use as calibration baseline.
audit_note: Only the Turtel paper was checked in full (its text supports ReMax 0.190, o1 0.202, ECE 0.062 vs 0.093, market 0.151, plain GRPO overconfidence); Lee et al. not opened.

claim: Agent scaffolds reach crowd level on the RTF test set (0.170 vs crowd 0.172); ensembling helps agents (0.169 vs 0.180) but not base LMs.
agent_test: Sample-ensemble helps only with diverse samples; test.

claim: Frontier model progress shows steady Brier decrease: Sonnet 3.5 0.1925 to Sonnet 4 0.1560 on pastcasting (p=0.0024); neighbours often not distinguishable (effective n about 179).
agent_test: Use a pastcasting set with replayed retrieval to rank our schema variants.
audit_note: Minor: the decline is not monotonic (Sonnet 4 thinking 0.1597 is above Sonnet 4 0.1560; Sonnet 3.7 0.1712 above 3.5 v2 0.1690), which the claim half-acknowledges; second source (Lu) does not contain these numbers.

claim: o3 scored 0.1352 vs Halawi crowd 0.149, but ten experts scored mean 0.157 and median 0.0225 on 157 questions: results are sensitive to mean vs median and question set.
agent_test: Report medians and means with CIs.

claim: Prompt effects are small: in Schoenegger et al.'s preregistered mixed-effects model only Bayesian-reasoning (+0.030) and propose-evaluate-select (+0.033) prompts differed significantly from control (both worse); frequency-based reasoning (-0.014) and base-rate-first (-0.011) were in the helpful direction but not significant after correction (significant only in a simpler t-test analysis at -0.019 and -0.016); the superforecaster-written conditional odds-ratio prompt was significantly worse than control.
agent_test: A/B base-rate-first vs Bayesian prompts in our schema.
audit_note: In Schoenegger et al.'s preregistered mixed-effects model the -0.014 (frequency-based) and -0.011 (base-rate-first) effects are not significant (adjusted p=0.774); they are only significant in the simpler t-test analysis (-0.019 and -0.016, adjusted p 0.022 and 0.036). The superforecaster-written prompt made forecasts significantly worse, not just no help.
claim_before_audit: Prompt effects are small: frequency-based reasoning (-0.014) and base-rate-first (-0.011) help; Bayesian-reasoning prompts and propose-evaluate-select hurt (+0.030, +0.033); superforecaster-written prompts did not help.

claim: Benchmark validity pitfalls are real: at least 3.8 percent of Halawi questions resolved early, over 10 percent trivial in Tao et al.; search returns post-cutoff content; Brier on mixed base rates misleads.
agent_test: Audit our evaluation sets for leaks and early resolution before trusting results.

claim: Consistency violations correlate with Brier (up to R about 0.9 for conditional checks), but the sign and size depend on check and dataset (negation arbitrage +0.60 on one set, -0.36 on another), and patching forecasts to pass the checks did not improve held-out checks or Brier.
agent_test: Use arbitrage checks in our loop as a cheap self-check and compare to later Brier.

claim: Diversity across models matters more than solo rank in an AI crowd at equal sample count (N=113, 101 allocations scored in-sample, no CIs). Not tested at equal tokens.
agent_test: Mix model families in the ensemble at equal total tokens.

claim: Market prices lag LLMs at long horizons but overtake near resolution; raw Brier needs a baseline.
agent_test: Report horizon-wise vs market baseline.

claim: As of 16 July 2026 FRI states several systems (Cassi AI, xAI, Google DeepMind) are statistically indistinguishable from the 2024 superforecaster median; Cassi outranks supers on market questions; 17 preliminary submissions rank above supers. Caveats: supers last elicited 2024, CIs overlap; parity, not outperformance. On Cassi's own Jul 2026 board the superforecaster median is still rank 1 (69.2 vs 68.8 Brier Index).
agent_test: Treat parity as reached on this benchmark; the open question is outperformance on fresh questions.

claim: Correction of the earlier refutation: the brief's numbers do come from FRI posts. 0.017 = 0.103 (best LLMs) minus 0.086 (supers) in the Brier Index post; the 2025-10-08 post gave gap 0.020 and linear parity in November 2026 (CI Dec 2025 to Jan 2028); the Brier Index post moved parity to March 2027. Both projections were overtaken by the July 2026 statement that several systems are already statistically indistinguishable. Karger Table 26 also has 0.017 at the 7-day horizon, by coincidence.
agent_test: None.

claim: Equal-token comparison of the parity-reaching systems is impossible from public data: ForecastBench imposes and records no token, tool or retrieval limits; Cassi, xAI and DeepMind methods are unpublished beyond a one-paragraph FRI description; Torchcast describes only a proprietary multi-agent pipeline using its own trained models plus commercial LLMs.
agent_test: Log tokens, tool calls and cost per question in our own harness; compare only against the price-only and no-scaffold baselines we can run.
audit_note: FRI describes Torchcast as a proprietary multi-agent architecture using Torchcast-trained models plus commercial LLMs; no mention of reinforcement learning.
claim_before_audit: Equal-token comparison of the parity-reaching systems is impossible from public data: ForecastBench imposes and records no token, tool or retrieval limits; Cassi, xAI and DeepMind methods are unpublished beyond a one-paragraph FRI description; Torchcast describes only a multi-agent plus RL-trained pipeline.

claim: Reference compute scale: a frontier ReAct forecasting agent uses 80k-200k tokens and 0.14-0.55 USD per question; the best scaffolded pipeline in BTF-2 cost 1.68 USD; BLF used 50-100M tokens for 5 trials on 400 instances (about 125k-250k tokens per question, derived, about 0.6 USD); Metaculus bots spend 0.10-3 USD per question.
agent_test: Set a test budget of about 0.5 to 2 USD per question so results compare with the field.
audit_note: BLF per-question figure is a 5-trial total (25-50k per single run); 80-200k and 0.14-0.55 USD are in BTF-2 text, not in the d14 table.

claim: No paper isolates pipeline components at fixed compute. Measured gains at unmatched compute: agentic over non-agentic search 0.1182 to 0.1140; 10-sample mean over one sample 0.1182 to 0.1140; agentic supervisor 0.1199 to 0.1125; Platt 0.1119 to 0.1076; sub-question decomposition 0.141 to 0.132 (confounded: second model, extra compute, research done two days later); belief state +2 to +3 Brier Index on two backbones and none on a third; AIA-style LLM aggregator worse than a plain mean in Murphy's test.
agent_test: Run an ablation at matched tokens: single run, mean of N, N plus supervisor, N plus Platt.

claim: Most of the market-question edge is the supplied market price. A price-only submission scores Brier Index 81.5 on market questions; a leading agent adds +2.3 (not significant on 200 events); GPT-4.5 correlated 0.994 with the market; in AIA, price alone 0.096 vs agentic search alone 0.085 vs both 0.075, so own reasoning adds a real but smaller part.
agent_test: Always report a price-only baseline and the agent with and without the price.
audit_note: 'Most of the edge' is an interpretation; BLF +2.3 is nonsignificant per Murphy; numbers all check.

claim: Leakage: live ForecastBench is prospective, so it is not inflated by search leakage, but careful backtests still show 1.5% (BLF) to 1.65% (AIA) leaking search results, 7.0% of questions exposed, over 40% leaked generated questions, a 52% gap when prompts only pretend to forget, and parametric leakage for models with cutoffs after the question date (Opus 4.7). Whether 2025-26 backtest-based claims are inflated is not measured.
agent_test: Use live questions or a frozen corpus; use only models with cutoff before the question date.
audit_note: 1.5% is of retained search results (21/1377); BTF-2 notes Opus 4.7 (Jan 2026 cutoff) appeared to show parametric leakage.

claim: Frozen-corpus pastcasting is practical and sensitive (BTF-2: 1,417 questions, 15M documents, detects 0.004 Brier) but only a 20-question visual check ties it to live search. No study shows a frozen-corpus score predicts the live ForecastBench rank.
agent_test: Validate our pastcasting set by rank-correlating with a live ForecastBench submission.

claim: Consistency (arbitrage) checks are not shown to work as an inner-loop selector or target: patching passed trained checks but not held-out checks or Brier; RL on Brier reduced arbitrage violations by 15% as a side effect. No study tests consistency to choose among samples for one question.
agent_test: Use conditional and negation checks as a post-hoc audit and measure their correlation to Brier ourselves.

claim: Platt or extremising transfers only partly: fitted on another question set it keeps about 60% of the in-distribution gain (0.1125 to 0.1104 vs 0.1119 to 0.1071); sqrt(3) fixed beat supers and their own optimum (1.72); gains shrink when a market price anchor is given; one backbone showed no resolved gain. Transfer across models of different hedging is untested.
agent_test: Fit the scaling on one model and question mix; test on another model and a market-anchored mix.

claim: Model diversity vs more samples at equal tokens is untested. At equal sample count a mixed team beat a single-model team (113 questions, in-sample choice); at roughly equal cost (about 1.6 USD) a structured pipeline beat a plain four-agent mean by 0.006 Brier.
agent_test: Run: N samples of best model vs N/3 each of three families at equal tokens, with CIs.

claim: Horizon decay vs markets for 2026 models is not measured. 2025 evidence (Prophet Arena) shows markets lag LLMs far from resolution and overtake near it; ForecastBench cut dataset horizons from 8 to 5 on 2026-09-30, and BLF scored only 7, 30 and 90 days.
agent_test: Score our agent by lead time against the market price.

claim: Prompting on 2026 models: forecasting-tips guidance helped Gemini 3.1 Pro with fixed research (0.141 to 0.129) but not an Opus 4.6 agent (0.131 both); human review found over-strict base-rate extrapolation as a failure; no 2026 test of base-rate-first or frequency framing; raw news can hurt in some categories.
agent_test: Test base-rate-first with a disruption check on our agent; do not assume 2024 gains hold.

claim: ForecastBench changed scoring, sources, horizons and question mix repeatedly (difficulty adjustment 2025-10-07, combinations dropped 2025-10-17, Brier Index 2026-03-04, horizons cut 2026-09-30, Kalshi added, RAND and Manifold removed), so trend lines and parity dates mix different tests.
agent_test: Pin the benchmark version when quoting any number.
